title: Do Stationarity Transformations Actually Improve Time Series Forecasts? A Controlled Experimental Evaluation
summary: Stationarity transformations, such as differencing, are a common preprocessing step in forecasting, motivated by the idea that modifying a series to achieve stationarity improves accuracy. Whether this is true, and for which processes, has rarely been evaluated in controlled experiments. We study the decision to transform as the object of inquiry. We cross eighteen synthetic data-generating processes, most of them stochastic-trend processes spanning exact and near unit roots, fractional integration, seasonal unit roots, structural breaks, and heteroscedasticity, with ten transformations,…
